emma: hey all, first week check-in. running Ubuntu 22.04 on a personal laptop. trying to get ruby and python via asdf but the ruby build fails with an ssl cert/openSSL error. also curious if anyone on linux uses the nix overlay we mentioned during onboarding or should i just stick to asdf + apt? quick tips please 🙏

ryan: welcome! for Ruby on Ubuntu you usually need libssl-dev + zlib1g-dev before compiling. try:

ryan: ```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libreadline-dev libyaml-dev libsqlite3-dev sqlite3 libxml2-dev libxslt1-dev libffi-dev
ASDF_PYTHON_BUILD_OPTS="--enable-shared" asdf install ruby 3.2.2
```

ryan: the ASDF_PYTHON_BUILD_OPTS above is just an example for python builds — for ruby you might set flags like `RUBY_CONFIGURE_OPTS="--with-openssl-dir=/usr"` if you have a nonstandard openssl.

infra-bot: NOTE: If your machine is behind the corporate proxy, set `http_proxy`/`https_proxy` and `no_proxy` in your shell before running builders, otherwise curl/git downloads time out. Example: `export https_proxy=http://proxy.corp:3128` and `export no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1,.internal.redwood.com`

emma: i'm behind a home router only, no corp proxy. curious about nix — is it overkill? i like the reproducibility idea but worried about ramp.

ada: (ada) we have two supported paths: devcontainer (recommended) and local asdf. Nix is used by a small subset of infra folks; there's a maintained flake but it's not required. If you want reproducible envs across teammates, devcontainer or our docker-compose dev image are simplest.

ada: devcontainer image: `ghcr.io/redwood/dev/devcontainer:ubuntu-lts`. It mounts your dotfiles and supports ssh-agent forwarding. For signing commits with GPG in the container you can forward the agent: add `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and `GPG_AGENT_SOCK` mounts in your devcontainer config.

jesse: dotfiles tip: fork `github.com/redwood/dotfiles-template` and add `~/.local/bin` to PATH early. we also expect `~/.config/redwood/env` to hold non-sensitive runtime flags (ignored by git). for secrets use 1Password CLI: `eval $(op signin)` then `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(op item get "redwood/dev-token" --fields label=token)` and add to `direnv` config.

ryan: if you want to try nix, start with `nix develop` on the repo — it will drop you into the exact toolchain we use. but be mindful of docker interplay (nix and docker file mounts can be confusing on WSL).

emma: thanks — quick Q: where do i add my GPG pubkey and SSH pubkey for infra access?

jesse: upload SSH key to the internal portal under "Access -> SSH Keys". GPG pubkey goes in the same portal under "Signing Keys". After upload, ask infra to whitelist your key for CI artifacts (some repos require signed commits for releases).

infra-bot: REMINDER: Register your machine fingerprint at `https://infra.internal.redwood.com/machines` if you want to use internal docker registries without MFA popups.

emma: awesome — i'll try apt deps first, then devcontainer. i'll post logs if i hit the same openssl build error. thanks all :raised_hands:
